To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding affinity of HIV-1 TAR to Tat peptide is reduced by acetylation of Lysine residue at position 50 and increased by acetylation at position 51, and methylation at position 51 increases the binding affinity of TAR to Tat peptide.
N-acetylation of lysines 50 and 51 of Tat peptide results in significant reduction of binding affinity for HIV-1 TAR.
acetylation and methylation of lysine residue of Tat peptide have different effect on its interaction with HIV-1 Tat RNA, which is dependent on the position of the modification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of lysine acetylation and methylation on RNA binding proteins and provides insight into the mechanism of RNA-protein interaction.
the effect of N- acetylation and N- methylation of lysine residue of Tat peptide on its interaction with HIV-1 TAT RNA.
the effect of PTM of lysine residues in Tat peptide on the interaction with TAR RNA and has revealed the position specific effects on binding thermodynamics and kinetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N-acetylation of lysines at K50 and K51 position of Tat, results in significant reduction in binding affinity and dissociation rate constant.

N-acetylation of K50 and K51 of Tat peptide results in a significant reduction in binding affinity with large enthalpic effect and a minor change in kinetic parameters, however, N-methylation at the same positions leads to a significant change in the kinetic parameters and a marginal change in binding affinity.
the effect of PTM on binding affinity is position specific and the thermodynamic and kinetics parameters can vary in a wide range depending on the nature of PTM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of Tat peptide to HIV-1 TAR is affected by PTM at both K50 and K51.

acetylation and methylation of lysine residue of Tat peptide have a position specific effect on binding affinity to TAR RNA, which can be explained by the change in the kinetics of association and dissociations of peptide-RNA complex.
, N-acetylation of lysines at both the positions (K50 and K51) of Tat peptide resulted in significant decrease of the binding affinity with K50 acetylated Tat peptide showing more drastic effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, N-acetylation or N-monomethlation of lysine can have a profound effect on the interaction between RBPs and their target RNA.
, acetylation of K50 and K51 residues have different effects on the binding affinity of HIV-1 Tat peptide to TAR.
the effect of PTM on the binding of RBPs is highly position specific and the effect on binding affinity is not a direct consequence of changes in the thermodynamic parameters.
